title: Kung Pao Chicken
subtitle: Sichuan stir-fried chicken with peanuts and dried chilli
excerpt: The Sichuan classic: chicken wok-fried with dried chillies, Sichuan pepper, peanuts, and the hot, numbing, sour sauce that makes this one of the most complex and addictive dishes in Chinese cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kung pao chicken (宫保鸡丁, Gōngbǎo jīdīng) is one of the most internationally recognised dishes of Sichuan cuisine, named after Ding Baozhen, a Qing-dynasty official with the title gong bao (palace guardian). The dish consists of diced chicken marinated briefly in soy and rice wine, stir-fried at high heat with dried chillies, Sichuan peppercorns, and peanuts, and finished with a balanced sauce of soy, vinegar, and sugar. The defining characteristics are the 'málà' quality of Sichuan cuisine: the numbing heat of Sichuan pepper and the fiery heat of chilli, balanced by the slight sweetness and sourness of the sauce. The peanuts should be added last to retain their crunch.

content.text: Have the sauce mixed and all ingredients ready before the wok goes on the heat; the cooking is very fast and there is no time to measure once you start. The dried chillies must be cooked in the hot oil until darkened and fragrant before the chicken goes in; this blooms the chilli flavour into the oil. The Sichuan pepper should be added with the chillies.

content.text: Marinate the chicken in 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, and 1 tsp cornflour for 15 minutes. Mix the sauce: remaining soy, remaining wine, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and 1 tsp cornflour dissolved in 2 tbsp water.

Heat the wok over very high heat until smoking. Add the oil. Add the dried chillies and Sichuan pepper and fry for 20 seconds until darkened. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through.

Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onion. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce and toss to coat; it will thicken in about 30 seconds. Add the peanuts and toss. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
